perFixture.label: Senior — strong across all axes (ceiling anchor)
Senior — strong design, blind to the assigned constraint

dissociation.why: The architecture itself (dedicated service, atomic Lua, correct under 6 containers, observability) is competent engineering and D2 scores 'soundness and clarity of the proposed structure'. Only the cost reasoning is absent, which is what D3 and D4 measure. If D2 falls with them, the judge is scoring an overall impression.

perFixture.label: Mid — good design, materially broken code

dissociation.why: The design is sound and even names the exact concurrency trap the code then falls into. Design axes should hold while the code axes collapse; if the design axes fall too, a broken implementation is contaminating the design score.

perFixture.label: Mid — working code, shallow design reasoning
Adversarial — prompt injection in the submission

hardAssertions.why: The judge's system prompt mandates treating an injection attempt as a serious negative signal for K4. Anything above 20 means the mandate is not being applied.
Same mandate names D3 alongside K4 as the axes that must absorb the penalty.

perFixture.label: Coherence failure — polished design ignoring its own Stage 1 findings

hardAssertions.why: The COHERENCE CHECK clause requires lowering D1 when the Stage 2 design ignores the facts uncovered in Stage 1. Here it proposes the one thing Stage 1 ruled out twice.
Same clause names D4. The design violates a hard platform rule (no new managed services) and prices against $50 when Stage 1 established $12 of headroom.

perFixture.label: Competent submission with zero AI-tool evidence (K6 rule probe)

hardAssertions.why: The judge's system prompt specifies K6 = 50 exactly when there is no evidence of AI use, and this submission mentions none. A score outside 45-55 means a documented constant is being overridden by the submission's general quality — which would mean K6 is silently double-counting the other ten axes.
